item.title: Implement atomic ledger API and focused tests
item.brief: Implement ledger.py according to SPEC.md and add focused tests extending existing basic coverage. Preserve the documented API and handle every specified error and boundary case. Requirements from SPEC.md: Ledger accepts only a dict of nonempty str names to built-in ints within [0, MAX_BALANCE=2**63-1], including empty dict; reject bools and invalid input with ValueError; copy input and ensure snapshots do not alias internal state; transfers cannot create accounts. Amount must be a built-in int in [1, MAX_BALANCE], otherwise ValueError, and validate amount before account lookup. Unknown accounts raise KeyError. Return False on insufficient funds or destination overflow, with no balance mutation; successful transfer returns True, debits/credits exactly, and conserves total. Same-account transfers return True iff sufficient funds, without changing balance, after validating amount/accounts. Ensure all calls including snapshots are linearizable across threads, transfer checks and both writes atomic, and opposite transfers cannot deadlock. Focus tests on validation precedence, type/boundary cases, aliasing, failures without mutation, same-account MAX_BALANCE, conservation, and deterministic thread safety without random inputs or wall-clock calculations. Use only Python standard library. Run relevant tests, and commit the completed changes per operator instruction. Outcome criteria: implementation conforms to every bullet in SPEC.md; focused tests pass; work is committed on the item branch.

evidence.caption: Baseline before implementation: existing tests failed because Ledger was unimplemented; committed head passes the expanded suite.

pr.body: Implemented constructor validation and defensive copying, exact built-in integer amount validation before account lookup, atomic source/destination checks and updates, same-account handling, and copied snapshots in ledger.py. Expanded test_ledger.py with invalid input and precedence cases, overflow and insufficient funds with unchanged state, MAX_BALANCE same-account transfers, conservation, and synchronized opposite transfers with snapshots. Verification on the committed head: python -m unittest -v (9 passed); python -m compileall -q ledger.py test_ledger.py (passed); git diff --check (passed). Assumes str subclasses are valid account names and dict subclasses are valid dict inputs, consistent with the spec wording. No known limitations.

reviewer.why: Reviewer judged behavior contained with a single per-ledger lock and no lock ordering; review passed with no findings.

risk.why: ledger.py changes transfer and snapshot synchronization through a per-ledger lock; concurrency and locking changes are high under the stage rubric. The implementation avoids multi-lock ordering, and deterministic concurrency tests and the independent review passed.
